title: Proportional Sharing of Benefit Charges Among Base-Period Employers
content:
Under Employer Benefit Charging, each payment on a chargeable claim is shared among all of the claim's base-period employers in proportion to the wages each paid the claimant in the base period.

## The charge share

Each employer's charge share is its base-period wages divided by the claim's total base-period wages, rounded to four decimals. The claim's total base-period wages are the base-period wages from all employers recorded on the claim, for the base period as used by the claim's latest monetary determination; on a combined wage claim the total is the base-period wages of all states. On a combined wage claim only Lakeland wages make a Lakeland employer chargeable, but the denominator is the base-period wages of all states.

## The charge on a payment

The charge for a payment is the payment's gross payable amount multiplied by the employer's charge share and multiplied by the program charge share of its class — the regular-program charge share for regular claims, the Extended Benefits charge share for Extended Benefits claims — rounded to the cent. The regular-program charge share and the Extended Benefits charge share are figures set per charge class.

## When a charge is posted

A charge is posted only while the position status is noticed, responded, chargeable or protest pending. The status is read from the Department's record of that position.

| Position status | Charge posted from a payment |
|---|---|
| Noticed | Yes |
| Responded | Yes |
| Chargeable | Yes |
| Protest pending | Yes |
| Relieved | No |
| Closed | No |

## Relieved shares and reissued payments

- The share of a relieved employer is not shifted to the other employers; it goes to the state noncharge account.
- A reissued payment is not charged again, because the original charge stands.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A claim's total base-period wages are $41,200.00 and one employer paid $7,350.00 of them. Its charge share is 7,350 divided by 41,200, which is 0.178398…, rounded to four decimals: 0.1784.

- A regular-claim payment with a gross payable amount of $512.00, at a regular-program charge share of the whole: 512.00 multiplied by 0.1784 multiplied by 1 gives 91.3408, a charge of $91.34.
- An Extended Benefits payment of $512.00, at an Extended Benefits charge share of one half: 512.00 multiplied by 0.1784 multiplied by 0.5 gives 45.6704, a charge of $45.67.

The share is rounded first and the charge is then worked from the rounded share.
